subject: english
question: "The cycle continues. It's a vicious circle." The writer calls it a vicious circle because:

options.text: keeping old, broken stuff in our houses due to storage issues is a huge problem
the cycle of buying, throwing and again buying continues in a harmful way
we are helpless when things break and we can't do without them
we needed to buy new gadgets and their disposal is not our concern

solution:
The correct answer is **'****the cycle of buying, throwing and again buying continues in a harmful way'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given passage talks about the initiative called 'Repair Cafes' '*that allow local residents to fix household objects and electronics with the help and advice of enthusiastic volunteers.' which in turn reduces e-waste.*
 
• In the second paragraph of the passage it has been stated - 
 
 
• *"We're society of waste and overconsumption,"says Emmanuel Vallee, organiser of the Repair Cafe Paris, which typically sees around 25 people attending per event, including some online, since it launched in May 2019. "We throw things away that we don't need to and buy new gadgets before exploring the possibility of repair. The cycle continues. It's a vicious circle."*
 
 
 
• From this we can conclude that the writer calls it a vicious circle because people buy electronic goods, then throw them away when they no longer work and buy another one. When the damaged good is thrown away without repairing, it adds to the already inflated number of e-waste in the world which ultimately harm the environment. 
 
• Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.
